title: runner: first-class workflow enumeration (listWorkflows) with a future CLI list-workflows command

raw.title: runner: first-class workflow enumeration (listWorkflows) with a future CLI list-workflows command
raw.body:
## Problem

There is no designed way to enumerate the workflows of an Arazzo document. What exists today is low-level plumbing: `ArazzoDocument.workflowIndex` is a `Map<WorkflowId, JSONPointer>` built by `ArazzoDocumentRegistryProvider`, so a caller can do `[...document.workflowIndex.keys()]` — but only after going through a registry provider to obtain the document, and the index yields ids and pointers, not the workflow's `summary`/`description`. "What workflows does this document offer?" is the very first question a consumer (or a future CLI/UI) asks, and answering it currently requires internal knowledge of the registry/index machinery.

## Proposal

### Programmatic API

A first-class enumeration read on `ArazzoDocument`, consistent with the existing split of responsibilities (index building stays in the registry provider; the document class holds the parse result plus prebuilt indexes and exposes thin reads):

```ts
interface WorkflowDescriptor {
  workflowId: WorkflowId;
  summary?: string;
  description?: string;
  jsonPointer: JSONPointer;
}

class ArazzoDocument {
  // existing: readonly workflowIndex: ArazzoWorkflowIndex;
  listWorkflows(): WorkflowDescriptor[];
}
```

- `workflowId` and `jsonPointer` come straight from the existing `ArazzoWorkflowIndex`; `summary`/`description` are read lazily from the parse result at the indexed pointer (thin read — no new index building, no normalization/dereferencing).
- Deterministic order: document order (the order the index was built in).

### Scope decision: cross-document workflows

An entry document's `sourceDescriptions` may include Arazzo-typed sources whose workflows are addressable at runtime via `$sourceDescriptions.<name>.<workflowId>`. Options:

1. `listWorkflows()` stays strictly local to the document (proposed default — pure, synchronous, no source loading), and
2. a separate, registry-level enumeration (e.g. on the executor or registry) that includes reachable Arazzo sources, returning qualified references — can be follow-up work once there is a concrete consumer.

### CLI sketch (future `packages/cli`)

For the CLI package (currently a `-- Placeholder --` in the root README), the command wraps the API above:

```
arazzo list-workflows <document-uri> [--json]
```

- `<document-uri>` — local path or http(s) URL, resolved through the same registry/resolver machinery the runner uses.
- Default output — human-readable table:

  ```
  WORKFLOW ID        SUMMARY
  place-order        Place an order for a pet
  cancel-order       Cancel a previously placed order
  ```

- `--json` — machine-readable array of `WorkflowDescriptor` objects (without `jsonPointer` unless `--verbose`), suitable for piping into other tooling.
- Exit non-zero with a structured error message when the document fails to parse or is not an Arazzo document.

## Out of scope

- Describing a single workflow's requirements (inputs schema, security, servers) — covered by the workflow execution profile (#82); a future `describe-workflow` CLI command is a rendering of that profile, not of this API.
- Enumerating workflows across source descriptions (option 2 above) — follow-up.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ArazzoDocument.listWorkflows()` returns `workflowId`, `summary`, `description`, `jsonPointer` for every workflow, in document order, without triggering source-description loading or dereferencing.
- [ ] Absent `summary`/`description` are omitted/`undefined`, not empty strings.
- [ ] Exported from the package public API and documented in the runner README.
- [ ] Covered by tests against the existing fixtures, including a document whose workflows lack `summary`/`description`.
